<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 2 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Book 2 ==

== Biography ==

General Jinjur is the commander of the Army of Revolt, a force she assembled from all parts of the Land of Oz — Munchkin, Quadling, Winkie, and Gillikin recruits, each company distinguished by a different colored strip on their uniforms — marching at her express command against the Emerald City. Having taken the city, she moves from military commander to self-declared monarch: she is found seated on the Scarecrow's throne, wearing his second-best crown and holding the royal sceptre, eating caramels, and she declares that "the throne belongs to whoever is able to take it" and that she is now Queen, with anyone who opposes her guilty of treason. Fearing that the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman might join forces against her, she sends for the witch Old Mombi, offering her large rewards to prevent their return to the Emerald City.

== Relationships ==

'''[[The Scarecrow]]''' — enemy. Jinjur's unease over the Scarecrow's escape from the Emerald City, and their later confrontation in the throne room where he challenges her right to sit on his throne, suggest a rivalry between the two rulers.

'''[[Old Mombi]]''' — wary alliance. Jinjur summoned Mombi and promised her large rewards to help defend the rebel army against the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman, suggesting a tactical alliance forged out of shared need rather than trust.

'''[[Glinda the Good]]''' — enemy. Evidence tied to Jinjur's demand that Mombi be delivered up as a prisoner could indicate an antagonistic stance toward Glinda.

'''[[Jack Pumpkinhead]]''' — enemy. Jack's fear of being turned into tarts or soup at Jinjur's hands points to an adversarial dynamic, though this reflects his own apprehension rather than a confirmed fact.

'''[[Nick Chopper]]''' — enemy. Nick Chopper's remark that "Jinjur is still the Queen, and we are her prisoners" reflects the captor role she held over him and his companions.

== References ==

<references/>

=== Events ===

* He meets General Jinjur, leader of an all-girl Army of Revolt aiming to conquer the Emerald City from the Scarecrow King.
* Jinjur wants City's gems and treasury for her Army, tired of male rule.
* Tip follows Jinjur to a forest clearing where 400 girls, armed with knitting needles, assemble in four companies by home region (Munchkin, Quadling, Winkie, Gillikin).
* Jinjur addresses her Army, declares Revolt against men of Oz.
* The Scarecrow learns Jinjur's regiment of girls conquered the city because his Standing Army fled rather than fight.
* The Saw-Horse bursts through the gate, knocking over several of Jinjur's girl guards and the new Guardian of the Gate as the trio escapes the City.
* General Jinjur, fearing the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman joining forces against her rebel army, sends for the witch Mombi to stop their return to the Emerald City.
* In the throne room they find General Jinjur seated on the Scarecrow's throne, wearing his crown and eating caramels.
* The Scarecrow and Jinjur argue over the legality of her rule, while his companions offer mocking suggestions for dealing with her.
* Jinjur signals the Army of Revolt, who surround and disarm the group, seizing the Tin Woodman's axe and taking them prisoner.
* Jinjur threatens to destroy each companion in a gruesome way, while ordering Tip returned to old Mombi.
* The Scarecrow releases mice hidden inside his straw stuffing, sending the Army of Revolt and Jinjur fleeing the palace in panic.
* The Scarecrow argues that Jinjur is rightfully Queen and that the group has no claim to occupy her palace.
* Tip reports from the window that girl soldiers surround the palace, confirming they remain prisoners despite driving Jinjur out earlier.
* The Woggle-Bug and Jack Pumpkinhead voice fear of being eaten, since Jinjur threatened to turn them into tarts, goulash, or soup.
* The Scarecrow removes his crown, hands it aside, and reflects that Jinjur may now claim it.
* The Scarecrow explains that Jinjur's Army of Revolt seized the Emerald City and stole its emerald jewels, and asks Glinda for help.
* Queen Jinjur, alarmed by the army, sends a messenger asking Glinda's demands, and Glinda demands that Mombi be surrendered to her.
* Mombi tricks Jinjur by magically switching appearances with Jellia Jamb, so that Jellia is handed over to Glinda in Mombi's place.
* Glinda angrily demands the real Mombi, and Jinjur allows Glinda's search party to enter the city to look for her.
* Queen Jinjur despairs on learning Mombi confessed and that Tip is truly Princess Ozma.
* Jinjur refuses to give up her throne and declares war on Glinda and Ozma.
* Glinda, Ozma, the Scarecrow and a small guard fly the Gump into the palace courtyard and capture Jinjur.

<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 3 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Book 3 ==

== Biography ==

Jinjur is a dairy-maid encountered along the road, recognized by Ozma despite her humble occupation and greeting her with a curtsy as "your Highness." She had previously assembled an army of women, driven the Scarecrow from the throne of the Emerald City, and fought a battle against the powerful army of Glinda the Sorceress. By the time of this encounter, she has married a man who owns nine cows and describes herself as happy, contented, and willing to lead a quiet life, minding her own business.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Glinda the Good]]''' — enemy. Jinjur once fought a battle against Glinda's army, which could indicate a lasting rivalry between them.

'''[[Ozma]]''' — acquaintance. Ozma recognizes Jinjur on sight as a dairy-maid, suggesting the two are already familiar with one another.

'''[[Scarecrow]]''' — enemy. Jinjur once drove the Scarecrow from the throne of the Emerald City, suggesting an adversarial history between them.

=== Events ===

* Ozma's party, including Dorothy, Tiktok, and Billina, crosses the desert on the magic carpet and travels to the Emerald City, meeting Jinjur (now a contented farm wife) along the way.

<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 6 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Book 6 ==

== Biography ==

General Guph, referred to at times simply as the General or the Captain General, holds the rank of General. He is recorded returning to the cavern of the Nome King, where the King greets him with "Well, what luck? Will the Whimsies join us?" Guph answers, "They will," a reply that indicates he had been dealing with the Whimsies on the King's behalf and came back with a favorable answer.

In the company of Dorothy, the Wizard, the Shaggy Man, and the Tin Woodman, the Captain General takes part in a journey through Oz. He asks where the group is to go next, noting that "we haven't visited the Rigmaroles or the Flutterbudgets yet," and remarks that he is "glad we visited the Fuddles." Later, as the party crosses from the Gillikin Country into the Country of the Winkies, he calls out to note the change from purple to yellow hues, saying, "Aha! here is the Country of the Winkies. We are just crossing the boundary line."

During this same journey, the Captain General speaks favorably of the Wizard, telling Dorothy that "all the people of Oz...are very proud of their Wizard," and recalling that "he once made some soap-bubbles that astonished the world." He also asks whether the Scarecrow has heard of Ozma's trouble, a question the Wizard answers in the negative.

== Personality ==

General Guph presents himself as confident and assured of his own effectiveness. Reporting to the Nome King on his recruiting efforts, he answers plainly and without hesitation — "They will," and "Yes, indeed... I have their promise" — a directness that contrasts with the King's disbelief ("No!" cried the astonished King) and suggests Guph trusts his own success even when his superior does not share that confidence.

Among Dorothy's traveling companions, where he is addressed as the Captain General, Guph shows a more inquisitive and appreciative side. He asks where the party will travel next ("Where to?") and, as concern grows over Ozma's situation, presses for news of the Scarecrow ("Has the Scarecrow heard of Ozma's trouble?"), showing attentiveness to the group's unfolding troubles. He also voices open admiration for the Wizard, describing him as someone "all the people of Oz" take pride in, and expresses simple contentment with the day's outing ("For my part, I'm glad we visited the Fuddles.").

== Relationships ==

'''[[Roquat]]''' — employment. When General Guph returned to the cavern of the Nome King, his Majesty asked, "Well, what luck? Will the Whimsies join us?" — an exchange that suggests Guph serves the Nome King in a subordinate, employed capacity.

'''[[King]]''' — employment. A further exchange, "Very well, your Majesty. Do what you will with the girls for all I care," again seems to place Guph in service to a king, reporting outcomes and deferring to royal authority.

'''[[Dorothy]]''' — acquaintance. Guph, addressed here as the Captain General, is present when Dorothy and her companions discuss their travels — "What! Are we going to Fuddlecumjig?" asked the Captain General — suggesting at least a passing acquaintance between them.

'''[[Nick Chopper]]''' — acquaintance. In conversation the Captain General asks, "Has the Scarecrow heard of Ozma's trouble?" of the Tin Woodman, indicating a similarly casual, acquainted rapport.

'''[[Ozma]]''' — enemy. A note attributed to Guph, "Ozma is surely lost," could indicate an adversarial stance toward Ozma, though the phrasing alone offers only a tentative basis for this reading.

== Trivia ==

* Addressed as "Captain General" while traveling with Dorothy's companions, but simply as "General" or "Guph" when reporting to the Nome King.
* Traveled through Fuddlecumjig and the Country of the Winkies alongside Dorothy, the Wizard, the Shaggy Man, and the Tin Woodman.
* Returned to the cavern of the Nome King specifically to report on whether the Whimsies would join, answering "They will" when asked.
* Spoke proudly of the Wizard, noting that "all the people of Oz are very proud of their Wizard" and recalling that "he once made some soap-bubbles that astonished the world."
